works.title: lothea — On Love
works.summary: Gibran's sword and cross remain in view throughout the complete teaching. Its grain-floor and sacred fire stay beside the exact source, as do its fear and devotion.

works.title: phomila — On Children
works.summary: The opening paradox of belonging leads into the full bow-and-arrow passage, with Gibran's wording beside every Phi sentence.

works.title: loa — On Giving
works.summary: The teaching follows the prudent dog past the full well and orchard. Gibran's account of deservingness and gratitude remains intact, all the way to its closing wings.

works.title: riola — On Work
works.summary: Earth's pace and the worker's flute lead into a complete close translation. Cloth and bread keep company with stone and field until the voices of day and night close the teaching.
